comparison.objective: Distinct: use two-handed hedge shears to cut three target shoots while sparing flowers, then stow the tool, versus adjust and validate a shock absorber.
comparison.physical_skill: Both require bimanual coordination and damage avoidance, but shearing tests coordinated opposing handle motion, blade placement around targets and tool return. The candidate tests hex-key alignment, retained-collar adjustment, torque-limited relocking and iterative tuning from carriage dynamics.
comparison.success_condition: Record requires three cuts near target height, no flower cut, closed shears returned to the mat and arms at start; simulated severing is an angle/proximity trigger rather than contact cutting. Candidate requires two repeatable safe stops plus lock retention. Candidate does not quantify drift, excessive rebound or overload; the shears rubric does not specify applied cutting force, but these omissions do not imply duplication.
comparison.reason: Shared bimanual tool use is generic; target-selective cutting and stowage do not test dynamic damping adjustment, locking or repeated impact-response validation.
